title: Many coexisting attractors, a case study of the almost-conservative Hénon map
summary: For dynamical systems in the plane, there can be many periodic attractors coexisting in a bounded region. They become easier to find in systems with small dissipation, which we call ``almost-conservative''. We ask what happens when there are many periodic attractors. That is the vague question we start with. For a test study, we chose the Hénon map with a tiny dissipation. We tuned the other parameter to yield a case with 50 attracting periodic orbits.
